voice_note_label: Wing's own B2B outreach: one observation, plain, no pitch
style_notes: Write like one person noticing one thing, not like an agency.
Short sentences. Contractions. No adjectives about their business.
Never claim to have looked at anything except what the fact says.
End on a question that is easy to ignore.
banned_phrases: take your business to the next level
i hope this email finds you well
templates: Was reading your site and one thing stood out. Not a big deal on its own, but it is the kind of thing a customer would hit before you ever hear about it.
Small observation from your website. Figured you would rather know than not.
Noticed something on your site that is probably a five minute fix. Happy to point at it and leave you alone after that.
urgent_templates: This one is worth checking sooner rather than later.
Flagging this because it is live on your site right now.
fallback_frames: {fact} That is the kind of thing that quietly costs a business calls. Worth a look?
Was reading your site. {fact} Small thing to fix, easy thing to miss. Want me to point at it?
{fact} Not a crisis, but it is the sort of detail that adds up. Happy to show you where.
Noticed this while reading your site. {fact} Would it help to see what I would change first?
{fact} Most people never see that from their own side of the screen. Want the short version?
Quick one. {fact} Worth thirty seconds of your time to check.
{fact} If that is deliberate, ignore me. If it is not, it is a quick fix.
{fact} I only mention it because it is the first thing a customer would run into too.
{fact} Figured you would rather hear it from me than not hear it at all.
One thing from your site. {fact} Want me to send over what I would do about it?
